second_order: turning unusual old hardware into April Fools material
theme_note: Posters and commenters make genuine vintage equipment, an implausible purchase, and a beer image into the room's own April Fools material; what varies is whether they stage the premise, test if it is serious, identify the joke, or explain why they joined in.
Replies keep the fake-server premise going through browser, Ethernet, floppy-drive, beer, CD-writer, and Outlook jokes; one answer mixes the play with a factual PCI-card detail.

second_order: turning the old-server joke into real help and restoration
theme_note: The exchange moves from joking into explaining attachment to old machines, planning restoration, requesting and returning pictures, and arranging a free RAM gift; the practical help varies from information to pictures to a private material exchange.
A moderator applies the room's posting standard to one local April Fools joke; it belongs with no other slice-02 practice without blurring the distinction between making the joke and moderating it.

second_order: questioning who sent the r/place Discord ping
theme_note: One participant asks whether a compromised account was also behind an everyone-ping about r/place; the code stands alone because it questions attribution rather than showing the takeover practice itself.

second_order: calling homelab in to replace Homestuck with HOMELAB
theme_note: The surviving title, a moderator's prompt, and a direct call recruit the room into replacing Homestuck's work; what varies is whether the recruitment names takeover, leaves the action implicit, or states the replacement.

second_order: pushing back against taking Homestuck's banner
theme_note: Participants object, ask the group to move, offer a compromise, mock taking rather than building, restore the banner, or cooperate with restorers; these different turns share the practice of resisting or redirecting the takeover.

second_order: reporting the Homestuck banner changing hands
theme_note: Participants report that the canvas says homelab and explain that Homelab is taking Homestuck's logo; later slices may extend this theme when people recount the same episode after it ends.

second_order: celebrating having teamed together after r/place ended
theme_note: The aftermath mourns the finished canvas while participants call service an honour, celebrate teaming and banding together, and value a shared screen capture; the variation runs from loss to pride in having made something.

second_order: arguing over whether taking the logo was fair play
theme_note: Participants defend self-made rules, mock anger as salt, call the conduct childish, admit deliberate antagonism, send critics away, and attack either Homelab or its moderators; the common practice is contesting how the takeover should be judged, while positions remain opposed.

second_order: moderating insults in the r/place dispute
theme_note: A moderator removes an insulting comment under the room's rule and answers a later complaint with a ban; unlike the slice-02 low-effort removal, these actions police antagonistic exchange in the canvas aftermath.
